Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. ## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude-in-chrome

# Open-Trend-Tracker

Decision support for BMW product managers. The backend (`backend/`, Python, uv) unifies internal and
external data into a per-vehicle tree. The frontend (`frontend/`, Vite + React + TypeScript) is the PM planner; its API contract is `docs/API.md`.
Details are in `backend/README.md`.

## No LLM API in the pipeline (current version)

The pipeline is deterministic and makes no LLM calls. Do not add an LLM SDK or API calls. The work that
needs judgement is done here in the chat session, by editing the files below. A later version will
automate it through an API.

## Regenerating the data structure after a data update

1. New files go to `data/internal/` or `data/external/`. A new external format needs a small reader in
   `backend/app/external.py` (see `ev_market` for a table example). Then run `cd backend && uv run python -m app.unify`.
2. Read `data/unified/coverage.json` → `unmapped_labels`, grouped by source.
3. Curate `backend/taxonomy.json`:
   - add each customer-facing raw label, exactly as printed, to the `aliases` of the right attribute;
   - for free-text feature phrases, add a distinctive substring to `keywords` instead (the longest matching keyword
     wins). Then check `mapped_by: keyword` results for wrong matches and fix them with a longer keyword;
   - if no attribute fits, add a new attribute with `id`, `name` and `aliases` to the best category;
   - each alias may appear under only one attribute (the mapper raises an error on duplicates);
   - leave labels that are not product attributes unmapped on purpose: `no_class_found`,
     `General enquiry: customer feedback`, bare colour names (e.g. "Schwarz", "Mokka"), legal notes.
4. Turn raw external material into `data/external/<name>.jsonl` records, following the format in
   `backend/app/external.py`:
   - technical PDFs → `metric` records with `competitor` set when the fact is about another vehicle;
   - social media or review text → `comment` records with `label` and `sentiment`;
   - keep `url` and a short quote in `text` so every record stays traceable.
5. Bump `version` in `taxonomy.json` if the structure changed. Before regenerating a new version, move the old
   output to `data/unified_v<N>` so the two can be compared.
6. Rerun `unify` and `uv run pytest`. Report what changed: newly mapped counts, new attributes, labels left unmapped.

## Recommendation pipeline

`uv run python -m app.pipeline` runs steps 1-7 (see `backend/README.md`). Steps 3-4 use SYNTHETIC data
from `backend/app/dummy.py`. Never present those numbers as real, and replace them when real feeds arrive.
`backend/engineering_filter.csv` holds DUMMY engineer labels: engineers edit `feasible` on/off.
Figures are PDF only.

## Conventions

- Raw data in `data/` is confidential and gitignored. Never commit it and never publish it.
- Every observation must keep a `RawRef` (file + locator) back to its source.

"""Market-adjusted four-year event-study estimates for Chinese vehicle features.

Inputs are curated by hand in ``data/external/chinese_pairs/`` (every row carries a source URL):

- ``pairs.csv``        one row per version change: previous -> current version of one nameplate, with the
                       nameplate's first China launch (YYYY-MM) to detect a partial baseline year
- ``features.csv``     features new in the current version: detail, feature, subcategory, category
- ``model_sales.csv``  annual China sales per nameplate and source ``series``; a nameplate may have several
                       series (e.g. wholesale and registrations), and every change is taken within one series
- ``market_sales.csv`` annual China passenger-car retail (CPCA), total and NEV

Year alignment (annual data): a version launched in Jan-Mar sells in its launch year, so that is
year 1; a later launch makes the launch year a mixed year, so year 1 is the next calendar year.
The baseline is the calendar year before the launch year (previous version only). Year k is
year 1 + k - 1 and is observable when that calendar year is complete in ``market_sales.csv``
and the pair has a numeric baseline plus four annual observations. Partial baseline years and
later successor launches are retained as quality flags rather than silently dropping points.

Sales change is market-adjusted: excess = ln(S_k / S_base) - ln(M_k / M_base), with M the NEV
or ICE passenger market. SRNI-CAR observations use the total market aggregated from the same
monthly source, avoiding a denominator/provider mismatch. Repeated trim rows that reuse the same nameplate sales trajectory are
collapsed before estimation. On the balanced four-year panel, the coefficient for an item is
estimated after partialling out supported peer items, bundle size, powertrain, baseline scale,
calendar year and recorded data-quality flags. Standard errors are clustered by nameplate.

This is a dynamic, regression-adjusted difference-in-differences association. It is suitable for
screening observational product data, but it is not a causal claim: price, incentives, supply,
distribution, brand strength and unrecorded redesign changes may remain confounded.

Run from ``backend/``::

    uv run python -m app.analysis.chinese_pairs
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import math
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from app.paths import DATA_DIR, EXTERNAL_DIR
from app.analysis.srni_panel import SRNI_SERIES

INPUT_DIR = EXTERNAL_DIR / "chinese_pairs"
OUTPUT_DIR = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "chinese_pairs"
YEARS = (1, 2, 3, 4)
MIN_NAMEPLATES = 5
MIN_CLUSTERS = 10
MIN_RESIDUAL_DOF = 8
MIN_RESIDUAL_INFORMATION = 0.5
MAX_LOG_STANDARD_ERROR = 0.35
MAX_LEVERAGE = 0.8

CATEGORIES = (
    "Energy & Charging", "Driving Assistance", "Digital Cockpit & AI", "Vehicle Dynamics",
    "Smart Cabin", "Connected Ecosystem", "Smart Exterior", "General & Services",
)
# Middle layer between category and feature. Ids are shared with the news topics in
# app/services/impact_forecast.py.
SUBCATEGORIES = {
    "battery_range": ("Battery & range", "Energy & Charging"),
    "charging_replenishment": ("Charging & replenishment", "Energy & Charging"),
    "high_voltage_powertrain": ("High-voltage powertrain", "Energy & Charging"),
    "hybrid_powertrain": ("Hybrid & range-extender powertrain", "Energy & Charging"),
    "assisted_driving": ("Assisted driving", "Driving Assistance"),
    "perception_compute": ("Perception & driving compute", "Driving Assistance"),
    "autonomous_mobility": ("Autonomous mobility", "Driving Assistance"),
    "cockpit_intelligence": ("Cockpit intelligence", "Digital Cockpit & AI"),
    "displays_hmi": ("Displays & HMI", "Digital Cockpit & AI"),
    "vehicle_compute": ("Vehicle compute & E/E", "Digital Cockpit & AI"),
    "software_lifecycle": ("Software lifecycle & OTA", "Connected Ecosystem"),
    "cross_device_ecosystem": ("Cross-device ecosystem", "Connected Ecosystem"),
    "seating_comfort": ("Seating & occupant comfort", "Smart Cabin"),
    "cabin_entertainment": ("Cabin entertainment & audio", "Smart Cabin"),
    "passive_safety": ("Passive safety", "Smart Cabin"),
    "powertrain_performance": ("Powertrain & performance", "Vehicle Dynamics"),
    "ride_body_control": ("Ride & body control", "Vehicle Dynamics"),
    "by_wire_controls": ("Steer/brake-by-wire controls", "Vehicle Dynamics"),
    "body_manufacturing": ("Body structure & manufacturing", "Vehicle Dynamics"),
    "lighting_visibility": ("Lighting & visibility", "Smart Exterior"),
    "exterior_personalization": ("Exterior design & personalization", "Smart Exterior"),
    "ownership_services": ("Ownership & services", "General & Services"),
}


def read_csv(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def write_csv(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(rows[0]), lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)


def first_sales_year(launch: str) -> int:
    year, month = int(launch[:4]), int(launch[5:7])
    return year if month <= 3 else year + 1


def load(input_dir: Path = INPUT_DIR) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict], dict, dict]:
    pairs = read_csv(input_dir / "pairs.csv")
    features = read_csv(input_dir / "features.csv")
    ids = [p["pair_id"] for p in pairs]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("duplicate pair_id in pairs.csv")
    for f in features:
        if f["pair_id"] not in ids:
            raise ValueError(f"feature for unknown pair {f['pair_id']}: {f['detail']}")
        if f["subcategory"] not in SUBCATEGORIES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown subcategory {f['subcategory']!r} for {f['detail']}")
        if SUBCATEGORIES[f["subcategory"]][1] != f["category"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{f['subcategory']} belongs to {SUBCATEGORIES[f['subcategory']][1]}, not {f['category']}")
    sales: dict[str, dict[str, dict[int, int]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(dict))
    for row in read_csv(input_dir / "model_sales.csv"):
        sales[row["car_model"]][row["series"]][int(row["year"])] = int(row["units"])
    market = {int(r["year"]): {"NEV": int(r["nev_retail"]),
                               "ICE": int(r["total_retail"]) - int(r["nev_retail"]),
                               "TOTAL": int(r["total_retail"])}
              for r in read_csv(input_dir / "market_sales.csv")}
    srni_market_path = input_dir / "srni_market_sales.csv"
    if srni_market_path.exists():
        for row in read_csv(srni_market_path):
            market.setdefault(int(row["year"]), {})["SRNI_TOTAL"] = int(row["total_units"])
    return pairs, features, sales, market


def pick_series(by_series: dict[str, dict[int, int]], base_year: int, years: list[int]) -> str:
    """The series that has the baseline year and the most of the given years ('' if none has the baseline)."""
    covering = [(sum(y in values for y in years), name) for name, values in by_series.items() if base_year in values]
    return max(covering, key=lambda c: c[0])[1] if covering else ""


def pair_sales(pairs: list[dict], sales: dict, market: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Baseline and year 1-4 sales of each pair, raw and market-adjusted."""
    last_year = max(market)
    launches = defaultdict(list)
    for p in pairs:
        launches[p["car_model"]].append(p["current_launch"])
    rows = []
    for p in pairs:
        model, segment = p["car_model"], p["powertrain"]
        first = first_sales_year(p["current_launch"])
        base_year = int(p["current_launch"][:4]) - 1
        later = sorted(d for d in launches[model] if d > p["current_launch"])
        # a nameplate first sold after February of the baseline year has no full baseline year
        partial = p["nameplate_launch"][:7] > f"{base_year}-02"
        years = [first + k - 1 for k in YEARS if first + k - 1 <= last_year]
        series = pick_series(sales[model], base_year, years)
        chosen = sales[model].get(series, {})
        base = chosen.get(base_year)
        market_segment = "SRNI_TOTAL" if series == SRNI_SERIES else segment
        row = {"pair_id": p["pair_id"], "brand": p["brand"], "car_model": model, "powertrain": segment,
               "change_type": p["change_type"], "current_version": p["current_version"],
               "current_launch": p["current_launch"], "successor_launch": later[0] if later else "",
               "nameplate_launch": p["nameplate_launch"], "sales_series": series,
               "market_denominator": market_segment,
               "baseline_year": base_year, "baseline_sales": base}
        for k in YEARS:
            year = first + k - 1
            units = chosen.get(year) if year <= last_year else None
            superseded = bool(later and int(later[0][:4]) <= year)
            # the year exists only in another series: a change across series (e.g. wholesale vs
            # registrations) is not a sales change
            broken = units is None and any(year in v for v in sales[model].values()) and \
                any(base_year in v for v in sales[model].values())
            change = excess = None
            if (units and base and year in market and base_year in market
                    and market_segment in market[year] and market_segment in market[base_year]):
                change = units / base - 1
                excess = math.log(units / base) - math.log(
                    market[year][market_segment] / market[base_year][market_segment]
                )
            row[f"year_{k}"] = year
            row[f"sales_year_{k}"] = units
            row[f"change_pct_year_{k}"] = None if change is None else round(change * 100, 2)
            row[f"excess_log_year_{k}"] = None if excess is None else round(excess, 4)
            row[f"status_year_{k}"] = ("not_yet_observable" if year > last_year else
                                       "series_break" if broken else
                                       "missing_sales" if excess is None else "observed")
            flags = []
            if partial:
                flags.append("partial_baseline")
            if superseded:
                flags.append("successor_overlap")
            if series == "four_year_nameplate":
                flags.append("provider_change")
            row[f"quality_year_{k}"] = ";".join(flags)
        row["valid_four_year_pair"] = all(row[f"status_year_{k}"] == "observed" for k in YEARS)
        row["publication_eligible"] = (
            row["valid_four_year_pair"] and series != "four_year_nameplate" and not partial
            and not any("successor_overlap" in row[f"quality_year_{k}"] for k in YEARS)
        )
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


def _pct(log_value: float) -> float:
    """Convert a bounded log coefficient to a percentage without overflowing."""
    return round((math.exp(max(-20.0, min(20.0, log_value))) - 1) * 100, 2)


def independent_observations(pair_rows: list[dict], features: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """Collapse trim rows that reuse exactly the same annual nameplate trajectory."""
    membership: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
    parents: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for feature in features:
        pair_id = feature["pair_id"]
        for level, column in (("feature", "feature"), ("subcategory", "subcategory"), ("category", "category")):
            membership[pair_id][level].add(feature[column])
        parents[("feature", feature["feature"])] = (feature["subcategory"], feature["category"])
        parents[("subcategory", feature["subcategory"])] = (feature["subcategory"], feature["category"])
        parents[("category", feature["category"])] = ("", feature["category"])

    identity_fields = ["car_model", "powertrain", "sales_series", "market_denominator",
                       "baseline_year", "baseline_sales"]
    for year in YEARS:
        identity_fields.extend((f"year_{year}", f"sales_year_{year}"))
    grouped: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
    for pair in pair_rows:
        key = tuple(pair[field] for field in identity_fields)
        observation = grouped.setdefault(key, {
            "brand": pair["brand"], "car_model": pair["car_model"], "powertrain": pair["powertrain"],
            "sales_series": pair["sales_series"], "baseline_year": pair["baseline_year"],
            "market_denominator": pair["market_denominator"],
            "baseline_sales": pair["baseline_sales"], "pair_ids": set(),
            "publication_eligible": True,
            "items": defaultdict(set), "quality": defaultdict(set),
        })
        observation["publication_eligible"] = (
            observation["publication_eligible"] and pair["publication_eligible"]
        )
        observation["pair_ids"].add(pair["pair_id"])
        for level in ("feature", "subcategory", "category"):
            observation["items"][level].update(membership[pair["pair_id"]][level])
        for year in YEARS:
            for field in ("year", "sales_year", "change_pct_year", "excess_log_year", "status_year"):
                observation[f"{field}_{year}"] = pair[f"{field}_{year}"]
            observation["quality"][year].update(filter(None, pair[f"quality_year_{year}"].split(";")))

    observations = []
    for index, observation in enumerate(grouped.values(), 1):
        observation["observation_id"] = f"OBS{index:03d}"
        observations.append(observation)
    return observations, parents


def serializable_observations(observations: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Flatten analysis-only sets for the auditable CSV output."""
    rows = []
    for observation in observations:
        row = {
            "observation_id": observation["observation_id"], "brand": observation["brand"],
            "car_model": observation["car_model"], "powertrain": observation["powertrain"],
            "sales_series": observation["sales_series"], "pair_count": len(observation["pair_ids"]),
            "market_denominator": observation["market_denominator"],
            "publication_eligible": observation["publication_eligible"],
            "pair_ids": json.dumps(sorted(observation["pair_ids"])),
            "categories": json.dumps(sorted(observation["items"]["category"]), ensure_ascii=False),
            "subcategories": json.dumps(sorted(observation["items"]["subcategory"]), ensure_ascii=False),
            "features": json.dumps(sorted(observation["items"]["feature"]), ensure_ascii=False),
            "baseline_year": observation["baseline_year"], "baseline_sales": observation["baseline_sales"],
        }
        for year in YEARS:
            for field in ("year", "sales_year", "change_pct_year", "excess_log_year", "status_year"):
                row[f"{field}_{year}"] = observation[f"{field}_{year}"]
            row[f"quality_year_{year}"] = ";".join(sorted(observation["quality"][year]))
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


def _column_basis(matrix: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
    """Orthonormal basis for a possibly rank-deficient control matrix."""
    u, singular, _ = np.linalg.svd(matrix, full_matrices=False)
    if not len(singular) or singular[0] == 0:
        return np.empty((len(matrix), 0)), 0
    tolerance = max(matrix.shape) * np.finfo(float).eps * singular[0]
    rank = int(np.sum(singular > tolerance))
    return u[:, :rank], rank


def _unit_effect(log_effect: float, observations: list[dict], year: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Average and sample-total counterfactual units, counting each nameplate once."""
    by_nameplate: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    multiplier = 1 - math.exp(max(-20.0, min(20.0, -log_effect)))
    for observation in observations:
        by_nameplate[observation["car_model"]].append(float(observation[f"sales_year_{year}"]) * multiplier)
    per_nameplate = [float(np.mean(values)) for values in by_nameplate.values()]
    return round(float(np.mean(per_nameplate))), round(float(np.sum(per_nameplate)))


def isolated_effect(observations: list[dict], level: str, target: str, names: list[str], year: int) -> dict:
    """FWL event-study coefficient with nameplate-clustered uncertainty on a balanced panel."""
    balanced = [o for o in observations if o["publication_eligible"]
                and all(o[f"status_year_{k}"] == "observed" for k in YEARS)]
    target_values = np.array([target in o["items"][level] for o in balanced], dtype=float)
    treated = [o for o, value in zip(balanced, target_values, strict=True) if value]
    untreated = [o for o, value in zip(balanced, target_values, strict=True) if not value]
    treated_models = {o["car_model"] for o in treated}
    untreated_models = {o["car_model"] for o in untreated}
    clusters = {o["car_model"] for o in balanced}
    result = {
        "n_with": len(treated), "n_without": len(untreated),
        "nameplates_with": len(treated_models), "nameplates_without": len(untreated_models),
        "cluster_count": len(clusters), "residual_dof": None, "residual_information": None,
        "max_leverage": None, "status": "not_identified", "reason": "",
    }
    reasons = []
    if len(treated_models) < MIN_NAMEPLATES:
        reasons.append(f"fewer than {MIN_NAMEPLATES} treated nameplates")
    if len(untreated_models) < MIN_NAMEPLATES:
        reasons.append(f"fewer than {MIN_NAMEPLATES} control nameplates")
    if len(clusters) < MIN_CLUSTERS:
        reasons.append(f"fewer than {MIN_CLUSTERS} nameplate clusters")
    if not balanced:
        result["reason"] = "; ".join(["no complete four-year trajectories", *reasons])
        return result

    baseline = np.log(np.array([float(o["baseline_sales"]) for o in balanced]))
    baseline = (baseline - baseline.mean()) / (baseline.std() or 1.0)
    bundle_size = np.array([len(o["items"][level] - {target}) for o in balanced], dtype=float)
    bundle_size = (bundle_size - bundle_size.mean()) / (bundle_size.std() or 1.0)
    controls = [np.ones(len(balanced)), np.array([o["powertrain"] == "NEV" for o in balanced], dtype=float),
                baseline, bundle_size]
    calendar_years = sorted({int(o[f"year_{year}"]) for o in balanced})
    controls.extend(np.array([int(o[f"year_{year}"]) == value for o in balanced], dtype=float)
                    for value in calendar_years[1:])
    quality_flags = sorted(set().union(*(o["quality"][year] for o in balanced)))
    controls.extend(np.array([flag in o["quality"][year] for o in balanced], dtype=float) for flag in quality_flags)

    # Rare peer indicators are disclosed as part of the bundle but not assigned unstable coefficients.
    observed_models = {o["car_model"] for o in balanced}
    supported_peers = []
    for name in names:
        if name == target:
            continue
        with_name = {o["car_model"] for o in balanced if name in o["items"][level]}
        if len(with_name) >= MIN_NAMEPLATES and len(observed_models - with_name) >= MIN_NAMEPLATES:
            supported_peers.append(name)
    controls.extend(np.array([name in o["items"][level] for o in balanced], dtype=float)
                    for name in supported_peers)
    control_matrix = np.column_stack(controls)
    basis, control_rank = _column_basis(control_matrix)
    target_residual = target_values - basis @ (basis.T @ target_values)
    information = float(target_residual @ target_residual)
    full_rank = control_rank + (1 if information > 1e-10 else 0)
    dof = len(balanced) - full_rank
    result["residual_dof"] = dof
    result["residual_information"] = round(information, 4)
    if information < MIN_RESIDUAL_INFORMATION:
        reasons.append("feature is confounded with the launch bundle")
    if dof < MIN_RESIDUAL_DOF:
        reasons.append(f"fewer than {MIN_RESIDUAL_DOF} residual degrees of freedom")
    if reasons:
        result["reason"] = "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(reasons))
        return result

    outcome = np.array([float(o[f"excess_log_year_{year}"]) for o in balanced])
    outcome_residual = outcome - basis @ (basis.T @ outcome)
    coefficient = float(target_residual @ outcome_residual / information)
    residual = outcome_residual - coefficient * target_residual
    leverage = np.sum(basis ** 2, axis=1) + target_residual ** 2 / information
    result["max_leverage"] = round(float(np.max(leverage)), 4)
    if np.max(leverage) >= MAX_LEVERAGE:
        result["reason"] = "high-leverage observations prevent stable inference"
        return result

    # One-parameter FWL form of the CR1 nameplate-clustered covariance estimator.
    cluster_scores = []
    for cluster in sorted(clusters):
        mask = np.array([o["car_model"] == cluster for o in balanced])
        cluster_scores.append(float(np.sum(target_residual[mask] * residual[mask])))
    correction = len(clusters) / (len(clusters) - 1) * (len(balanced) - 1) / dof
    variance = correction * sum(score ** 2 for score in cluster_scores) / information ** 2
    standard_error = math.sqrt(max(0.0, variance))
    result["standard_error_log"] = round(standard_error, 4)
    if standard_error > MAX_LOG_STANDARD_ERROR:
        result["reason"] = "95% interval is too wide for publication"
        return result

    lower_log, upper_log = coefficient - 1.96 * standard_error, coefficient + 1.96 * standard_error
    mean_units, sample_units = _unit_effect(coefficient, treated, year)
    lower_units, lower_sample_units = _unit_effect(lower_log, treated, year)
    upper_units, upper_sample_units = _unit_effect(upper_log, treated, year)
    result.update({
        "status": "identified", "reason": "", "impact_pct": _pct(coefficient),
        "lower_pct": _pct(lower_log), "upper_pct": _pct(upper_log),
        "incremental_units": mean_units, "lower_units": lower_units, "upper_units": upper_units,
        "sample_incremental_units": sample_units,
        "sample_lower_units": lower_sample_units, "sample_upper_units": upper_sample_units,
    })
    return result


def impact(observations: list[dict], parents: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Conditional market-adjusted estimates from independent, complete four-year trajectories."""
    output = []
    for level in ("category", "subcategory", "feature"):
        names = sorted(set().union(*(observation["items"][level] for observation in observations)))
        for name in names:
            subcategory, category = parents[(level, name)]
            with_item = [o for o in observations if name in o["items"][level]]
            pair_ids = set().union(*(o["pair_ids"] for o in with_item))
            row = {
                "level": level, "name": name,
                "label": SUBCATEGORIES[name][0] if level == "subcategory" else name,
                "subcategory": subcategory, "category": category,
                "pair_count": len(pair_ids), "independent_count": len(with_item),
                "independent_nameplates": len({o["car_model"] for o in with_item}),
                "models": json.dumps(sorted({o["car_model"] for o in with_item}), ensure_ascii=False),
            }
            results = []
            for year in YEARS:
                result = isolated_effect(observations, level, name, names, year)
                results.append(result)
                for key in (
                    "impact_pct", "lower_pct", "upper_pct", "incremental_units", "lower_units", "upper_units",
                    "sample_incremental_units", "sample_lower_units", "sample_upper_units", "n_with", "n_without",
                    "nameplates_with", "nameplates_without", "cluster_count", "residual_dof",
                    "residual_information", "max_leverage", "standard_error_log",
                ):
                    row[f"{key}_year_{year}"] = result.get(key)
            row["identification_status"] = "identified" if all(r["status"] == "identified" for r in results) \
                else "not_identified"
            row["identification_reason"] = "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(
                reason for result in results for reason in result["reason"].split("; ") if reason
            ))
            output.append(row)
    return output


def plot(impact_rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    rows = [r for r in impact_rows if r["level"] == "subcategory" and r["impact_pct_year_1"] is not None]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["impact_pct_year_1"])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 0.35 * len(rows) + 1.6))
    if not rows:
        ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "No subcategory estimate passed the identification and uncertainty gates",
                ha="center", va="center", transform=ax.transAxes)
        ax.set_axis_off()
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        ax.plot([r["lower_pct_year_1"], r["upper_pct_year_1"]], [i, i], color="#7b8794", lw=1.5)
        ax.plot(r["impact_pct_year_1"], i, "o", color="#2f78a7")
    ax.axvline(0, color="#333", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(rows)), [f"{r['label']} ({r['nameplates_with_year_1']} nameplates)" for r in rows],
                  fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year-1 conditional market-adjusted sales effect (%), clustered 95% interval")
    ax.set_title("Independent Chinese sales trajectories: conditional subcategory effect", fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(path)
    plt.close(fig)


def run(input_dir: Path = INPUT_DIR, output_dir: Path = OUTPUT_DIR) -> dict:
    pairs, features, sales, market = load(input_dir)
    pair_rows = pair_sales(pairs, sales, market)
    observations, parents = independent_observations(pair_rows, features)
    observation_rows = serializable_observations(observations)
    impact_rows = impact(observations, parents)
    write_csv(pair_rows, output_dir / "pair_sales.csv")
    write_csv(observation_rows, output_dir / "independent_observations.csv")
    write_csv(features, output_dir / "feature_log.csv")
    write_csv(impact_rows, output_dir / "impact.csv")
    plot(impact_rows, output_dir / "plots" / "impact_by_subcategory.pdf")
    summary = {
        "pairs": len(pairs),
        "brands": len({p["brand"] for p in pairs}),
        "launch_range": [min(p["current_launch"] for p in pairs), max(p["current_launch"] for p in pairs)],
        "features": len(features),
        "observed_pairs_by_year": {k: sum(r[f"status_year_{k}"] == "observed" for r in pair_rows) for k in YEARS},
        "valid_four_year_pairs": sum(r["valid_four_year_pair"] for r in pair_rows),
        "collection_target": 200,
        "independent_observations": len(observations),
        "independent_nameplates": len({o["car_model"] for o in observations}),
        "complete_four_year_observations": sum(all(o[f"status_year_{k}"] == "observed" for k in YEARS)
                                               for o in observations),
        "complete_four_year_nameplates": len({o["car_model"] for o in observations
                                               if all(o[f"status_year_{k}"] == "observed" for k in YEARS)}),
        "publication_eligible_observations": sum(bool(o["publication_eligible"]) for o in observations),
        "publication_eligible_nameplates": len({o["car_model"] for o in observations
                                                if o["publication_eligible"]}),
        "estimated_items": {level: sum(r["level"] == level and r["identification_status"] == "identified"
                                               for r in impact_rows)
                            for level in ("feature", "subcategory", "category")},
        "last_full_sales_year": max(market),
    }
    (output_dir / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return summary


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps(run(), indent=2))

"""Seed reproducible four-year benchmark pairs.

These are historical China nameplate updates with a complete pre-update baseline
and four annual post-update observations. They are kept separate from the live
discovery rows so the page can be rebuilt from source-linked evidence.

Run from ``backend/``::

    uv run python -m app.analysis.four_year_seeds
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from pathlib import Path

from app.paths import EXTERNAL_DIR
from app.analysis.srni_panel import (
    SRNI_DOWNLOAD,
    SRNI_SERIES,
    SRNI_SALES,
    SRNI_UPDATES,
)

INPUT_DIR = EXTERNAL_DIR / "chinese_pairs"
SERIES = "four_year_nameplate"

SOURCES = {
    "Aion S": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aion_S",
    "Aion V": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aion_V",

    "Geely Boyue": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geely_Boyue",
    "Lynk & Co 03": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynk_%26_Co_03",
    "NIO ES6": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nio_ES6",
    "NIO ES8": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nio_ES8",
    "Haval H6": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haval_H6",
    "Roewe i5": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roewe_i5",
    "XPeng P7": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPeng_P7",
    "Wuling Hongguang Mini EV": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuling_Hongguang_Mini_EV",
    "XPeng G3": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPeng_G3",
    "Neta V": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neta_V",
    "Baojun RS-3": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baojun_RS-3",
    "Chery Tiggo 7": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chery_Tiggo_7",
    "Chevrolet Menlo": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevrolet_Menlo",
    "Buick Envision": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buick_Envision",
    "Buick GL8": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buick_GL8",
    "Lynk & Co 05": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynk_%26_Co_05",
    "Exeed TX": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exeed_TX",
    "Geely Jiaji": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geely_Jiaji",
    "Geely Xingrui": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geely_Xingrui",
    "Ora Good Cat": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ora_Good_Cat",
    "Neta U": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neta_U",
    "Geometry A": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometry_A",
    "Leapmotor T03": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leapmotor_T03",
    "BYD Song Max": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYD_Song_Max",
    "Changan CS75": "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changan_CS75",
        "features": [
            ("BlueCore NE 1.4T engine and seven-speed wet DCT", "Turbocharged powertrain upgrade", "powertrain_performance", "Vehicle Dynamics", "Changan's annual report documents the 2021 model's powertrain"),
            ("inCall 3.0S interactive system", "Upgraded cockpit computing", "cockpit_intelligence", "Digital Cockpit & AI", "Changan's annual report documents the connected interactive system"),
            ("540-degree camera, ACC stop-and-go, and lane-departure warning", "Advanced driver assistance", "assisted_driving", "Driving Assistance", "Changan's annual report lists the camera and assistance package"),
        ],
    },
    {
        "brand": "Changan", "model": "Changan UNI-K", "powertrain": "NEV",
        "previous": "UNI-K 2.0T", "current": "UNI-K iDD", "launch": "2022-03-10",
        "source": "https://www.autohome.com.cn/news/202203/1239837.html",
        "features": [
            ("Blue Whale 1.5T iDD plug-in-hybrid system", "New hybrid system", "hybrid_powertrain", "Energy & Charging", "The launch identifies UNI-K iDD as Changan's first production model with the iDD system"),
            ("30.7 kWh battery and 130 km NEDC electric range", "Longer-range battery", "battery_range", "Energy & Charging", "The launch documents the battery and electric-only range"),
        ],
    },
]


ALL_CURATED_UPDATES = [
    *CURATED_UPDATES, *TARGET_UPDATES, *EXPANSION_UPDATES,
    *VERIFIED_PANEL_UPDATES, *SRNI_UPDATES,
]


def _read(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def _write(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(rows[0]), lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)


def sync(input_dir: Path = INPUT_DIR) -> dict[str, int]:
    pairs = [row for row in _read(input_dir / "pairs.csv") if not row["pair_id"].startswith("FY")]
    features = [row for row in _read(input_dir / "features.csv") if not row["pair_id"].startswith("FY")]
    sales = [row for row in _read(input_dir / "model_sales.csv")
             if row["series"] not in {SERIES, SRNI_SERIES}]

    for index, update in enumerate(ALL_CURATED_UPDATES, 1):
        pair_id = f"FY{index:03d}"
        pairs.append({
            "pair_id": pair_id, "brand": update["brand"], "car_model": update["model"],
            "powertrain": update["powertrain"],
            "change_type": update.get("change_type", "historical_update"),
            "nameplate_launch": update.get("nameplate_launch", NAMEPLATE_LAUNCH.get(update["model"], "")),
            "previous_version": update["previous"],
            "previous_launch": update.get("previous_launch", "2020-01-01"),
            "current_version": update["current"], "current_launch": update["launch"],
            "source_url": update["source"],
        })
        for detail, feature, subcategory, category, evidence in update["features"]:
            features.append({
                "pair_id": pair_id, "detail": detail, "feature": feature,
                "subcategory": subcategory, "category": category, "evidence": evidence,
                "source_url": update["source"],
            })

    for model, values in SALES.items():
        for year, units in zip(range(2020, 2026), values, strict=True):
            sales.append({
                "car_model": model, "year": year, "units": units, "series": SERIES,
                "source": "Cited annual nameplate sales table", "url": SOURCES[model],
                "note": "Six-year continuous benchmark series; provider changes inside the source table are a quality caveat",
            })
    for model, by_year in IRREGULAR_SALES.items():
        for year, units in by_year.items():
            sales.append({
                "car_model": model, "year": year, "units": units, "series": SERIES,
                "source": "Cited annual nameplate sales table", "url": SOURCES[model],
                "note": "Continuous available benchmark series; provider changes inside the source table are a quality caveat",
            })
    for model, by_year in SRNI_SALES.items():
        for year, units in by_year.items():
            sales.append({
                "car_model": model, "year": year, "units": units, "series": SRNI_SERIES,
                "source": "SRNI-CAR peer-reviewed monthly vehicle-series dataset",
                "url": SRNI_DOWNLOAD,
                "note": "Annual sum of monthly sales for the exact source series in srni_car_manifest.json; no imputation",
            })

    market = _read(input_dir / "market_sales.csv")
    if not any(row["year"] == "2020" for row in market):
        market.append({
            "year": 2020, "total_retail": 19605000, "nev_retail": 1109000,
            "source": "CPCA full-year 2020 locally produced passenger vehicle retail; NEV retail benchmark",
            "url": "https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/market-industry/china-pv-retail-sales-likely-to-grow-8-in-2021-cpca-70017929",
        })
        market.sort(key=lambda row: int(row["year"]))

    _write(input_dir / "pairs.csv", pairs)
    _write(input_dir / "features.csv", features)
    _write(input_dir / "model_sales.csv", sales)
    _write(input_dir / "market_sales.csv", market)
    return {
        "seed_pairs": len(ALL_CURATED_UPDATES),
        "seed_features": sum(len(update["features"]) for update in ALL_CURATED_UPDATES),
        "sales_rows": (len(SALES) * 6 + sum(len(rows) for rows in IRREGULAR_SALES.values())
                       + sum(len(rows) for rows in SRNI_SALES.values())),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(sync())

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

搜索结果显示,全新一代起亚K3在中国的上市时间是**2019年5月16日**,而不是3月。我没有找到2019年3月上市的说法,这一点需要更正。另外,结果中也没有明确证实中国2019款配备UVO。

**上市与售价**
- 东风悦达起亚的全新一代K3于2019年5月16日晚正式上市,共推出两种动力共计7款车型,售价区间为9.88-12.88万元。
- 具体指导价为:1.5L+CVT智行版9.88万、舒适版10.38万、新锐版10.88万、智享互联版11.58万、智享智驾版12.28万、豪华版12.88万;1.4T+7DCT智享运动版12.58万(数据来源:凤凰网汽车)。

**尺寸与动力**
- 新车长宽高分别为4660/1780/1450毫米,轴距为2700毫米。
- 动力分为1.5L自然吸气加CVT和1.4T加7速双离合两种(见上方售价表)。

**配置**
- 内饰基本延续了海外版车型的设计,包括换装全新样式的多功能方向盘、悬浮式中控屏、倒梯形空调出风口等。
- 舒适配置包括前排座椅通风/加热、方向盘加热、驾驶模式选择、自动启停、换挡拨片、液晶仪表盘显示屏等。
- 高配车型外观方面……(注:此处原文未展开)。安全方面,高配还配有盲区检测、前方防碰撞预警和车道保持辅助、车道偏离预警等实用的辅助驾驶功能。(该段来自2021年的K3 EV报道,仅供参考,不针对2019款燃油版。)

**关于UVO**
- UVO是起亚的车载互联系统。搜索结果中能找到的UVO相关信息主要来自韩国市场:2012年款K3在准中型车中首次搭载了UVO系统;另一份韩国报道提到,新款K3内配10.25英寸大尺寸UVO导航屏幕,但该报道是2021年的改款车型。
- 因此,我无法从这些结果确认中国2019款全新K3的UVO配置情况,以及各配置等级是否包含UVO。建议直接查询东风悦达起亚官网或当年的官方配置表。

# Research brief: dated China version changes for SRNI-CAR vehicle series

You are researching, for each China vehicle series (车系) in your group file, ONE dated version change
(new generation, facelift / 中期改款, or model-year update / 年款 with a press launch) launched in
China inside the series' "allowed current_launch" range(s). Use WebSearch and WebFetch only. Do not
read or run anything in /private/tmp other than your group file and writing your output file.

For each series, return either a RECORD or a SKIP.

## Rules for a RECORD (all must hold)

1. current_launch (the China market launch / 上市 date, YYYY-MM-DD if known else YYYY-MM) falls in an
   allowed range for that series. Pre-sales, auto-show debuts and production starts do NOT count; use the
   official market launch (上市). If unsure about the date, say so.
2. You actually fetched (WebFetch) a dated launch article that states the launch and WHAT was added. Good
   sources: OEM press releases / OEM China newsroom, people.com.cn, chinanews, xinhuanet, sina auto,
   sohu auto, ifeng auto, autohome, yiche/bitauto, pcauto, xcar, Gasgoo (autonews.gasgoo.com),
   carnewschina, CnEVPost, annual reports. Wikipedia only if the sentence carries a citation, and then
   prefer the cited article. If a page cannot be fetched, find another that can.
3. Features are things NEW in this version relative to the previous one, stated in the article. Never
   infer features from sales. Give 2-4 features, the most salient ones. Do not include carried-over
   equipment.
4. Later-update check: search for any later China launch of the SAME nameplate between current_launch and
   31 Dec of the year4 shown for the chosen range. Report every one you find (full new generation,
   facelift, or new powertrain variant sold under the same series name) with date. If a FULL NEW
   GENERATION (or a renamed successor that replaced it under the same series) launched in that interval,
   the series is a SKIP (or choose a different allowed range where that is not the case).
5. nameplate_launch = the YYYY-MM when this nameplate (series name) was first sold in China (the line's
   first China launch, any generation). Must be on or before February of the baseline year shown for the
   range; otherwise SKIP.
6. Also give previous_version (short label of what sold in the baseline year) and previous_launch (YYYY-MM).

## Feature naming (reuse EXACTLY one of these; feature | subcategory | category)

- Advanced driver assistance | assisted_driving | Driving Assistance   (AEB, ACC, LKA, BSD, FCW, TJA...)
- Parking assistance | assisted_driving | Driving Assistance           (360 camera, auto-park, radar+camera)
- Larger or extra displays | displays_hmi | Digital Cockpit & AI         (digital cluster, bigger centre screen)
- Head-up display (HUD/AR-HUD) | displays_hmi | Digital Cockpit & AI
- New infotainment OS | cockpit_intelligence | Digital Cockpit & AI       (new named system: e.g. Lin OS, GKUI)
- Connected cockpit upgrade | cockpit_intelligence | Digital Cockpit & AI (telematics/4G connected services)
- AI voice assistant | cockpit_intelligence | Digital Cockpit & AI        (voice control)
- Cross-device phone integration | cross_device_ecosystem | Connected Ecosystem (CarPlay, CarLife, mirroring)
- Wireless device charging | cross_device_ecosystem | Connected Ecosystem
- Remote vehicle control | cross_device_ecosystem | Connected Ecosystem  (app remote start/lock/climate)
- Whole-vehicle OTA capability | software_lifecycle | Connected Ecosystem
- Turbocharged powertrain upgrade | powertrain_performance | Vehicle Dynamics (new turbo engine)
- Powertrain calibration update | powertrain_performance | Vehicle Dynamics   (new gearbox, new NA engine, emissions upgrade)
- New hybrid system | hybrid_powertrain | Energy & Charging                (HEV/PHEV added)
- Longer-range battery | battery_range | Energy & Charging
- Ride and chassis update | ride_body_control | Vehicle Dynamics          (new platform, suspension change)
- Adaptive suspension and AWD | ride_body_control | Vehicle Dynamics
- Brake-by-wire control | by_wire_controls | Vehicle Dynamics            (EPB + auto-hold, brake upgrades)
- Lighting and exterior redesign | lighting_visibility | Smart Exterior   (LED/matrix lamps, DRL)
- Exterior design personalization | exterior_personalization | Smart Exterior (new styling/front face/body)
- Cabin design and material upgrade | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin      (new dashboard, materials, interior redesign)
- Seat ventilation/heating/massage | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin
- Seating flexibility upgrade | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin
- Cabin air quality upgrade | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin               (PM2.5 filter, ionizer)
- Panoramic sunroof | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin
- Expanded active and passive safety | passive_safety | Smart Cabin      (extra airbags, stronger body, C-NCAP)
- Premium audio system | cabin_entertainment | Smart Cabin
- Flexible three-row seating | seating_comfort | Smart Cabin

## Output

Write a JSON array to the output file named in your task (one object per series, in input order):

```
{"srni": "<车系 exactly>", "decision": "record"|"skip", "skip_reason": "...",
 "brand": "English brand e.g. Volkswagen", "model": "English nameplate e.g. Volkswagen Magotan",
 "powertrain": "ICE"|"NEV", "nameplate_launch": "YYYY-MM", "previous_version": "...", "previous_launch": "YYYY-MM",
 "current_version": "...", "current_launch": "YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM", "source_url": "<one fetched URL>",
 "features": [["<detail in source's own terms, English>", "<feature>", "<subcategory>", "<category>",
               "<one-sentence evidence: what the dated article states, paraphrased; may include a short quote <=12 words>"]],
 "later_updates_in_window": "e.g. 'facelift 2020-06 (url)' or 'none found'",
 "confidence": "high|medium|low", "notes": "..."}
```

powertrain is NEV only for a pure EV / PHEV series. Be honest: if you cannot document what changed with a
fetched dated source, SKIP. Quality over quantity, but do try every series in your group. Your final
message: a short summary (records/skips) and the output file path.

"""Append accepted SRNI records to srni_panel.py and the manifest series_map.

usage: python3 -I integrate.py <srni_agg.json> <accepted.json> <worktree> <block comment>
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

agg_path, accepted_path, worktree, comment = sys.argv[1:5]
agg = json.load(open(agg_path))["series"]
records = json.load(open(accepted_path))
wt = Path(worktree)
panel = wt / "backend/app/analysis/srni_panel.py"
manifest_path = wt / "data/external/chinese_pairs/srni_car_manifest.json"
manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
source = panel.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def first_sales_year(launch):
    return int(launch[:4]) if int(launch[5:7]) <= 3 else int(launch[:4]) + 1


sales_lines, event_lines = [], []
for r in records:
    model, srni = r["model"], r["srni"]
    if model in manifest["series_map"] or srni in manifest["series_map"].values():
        raise SystemExit(f"already mapped: {model} / {srni}")
    if f'"{model}":' in source:
        raise SystemExit(f"already in SRNI_SALES: {model}")
    series = agg[srni]
    years = {int(y): v for y, v in series["years"].items()}
    months = {int(y): v for y, v in series["months"].items()}
    launch = r["current_launch"]
    base = int(launch[:4]) - 1
    first = first_sales_year(launch)
    window = [base] + [first + k for k in range(4)]
    if window[-1] > 2022:
        raise SystemExit(f"{model}: year 4 beyond SRNI coverage")
    if not all(months.get(y) == 12 and years.get(y, 0) > 0 for y in window):
        raise SystemExit(f"{model}: incomplete SRNI months in {window}")
    if r["nameplate_launch"][:7] > f"{base}-02":
        raise SystemExit(f"{model}: partial baseline ({r['nameplate_launch']} vs base {base})")
    for f in r["features"]:
        if len(f) != 5:
            raise SystemExit(f"{model}: malformed feature {f}")
    by_year = ", ".join(f"{y}: {years[y]}" for y in sorted(years))
    sales_lines.append(f'    "{model}": {{{by_year}}},')
    feats = "\n".join(
        "               (" + ", ".join(json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False) for x in f) + "),"
        for f in r["features"])
    event_lines.append(
        f'    _event({json.dumps(r["brand"], ensure_ascii=False)}, {json.dumps(model, ensure_ascii=False)}, '
        f'"{r["powertrain"]}", "{r["nameplate_launch"]}", {json.dumps(r["previous_version"], ensure_ascii=False)}, '
        f'"{r["previous_launch"]}", {json.dumps(r["current_version"], ensure_ascii=False)}, "{launch}",\n'
        f'           {json.dumps(r["source_url"], ensure_ascii=False)}, [\n{feats}\n           ]),')
    manifest["series_map"][model] = srni

marker = "}\n\n\ndef _event("
assert source.count(marker) == 1
source = source.replace(marker, "\n".join(sales_lines) + "\n" + marker)
source = source.rstrip("\n") + f"\n\n# {comment}\nSRNI_UPDATES.extend([\n" + "\n".join(event_lines) + "\n])\n"
panel.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"added {len(records)} series")

"""Exploratory, NOT publication-gated: sales association of launch bundles that contain an item.

Same panel and market adjustment as app.analysis.chinese_pairs, but the item is NOT separated from the
rest of its launch bundle (no peer-item or bundle-size controls) and there is no interval-width gate.
Controls kept: intercept, NEV, standardized log baseline, calendar-year dummies, data-quality flags.
Uncertainty: CR1 nameplate-clustered. Gates kept: >=5 treated and >=5 control nameplates, dof >= 8.

Panels:
  eligible  publication-eligible trajectories only (single source, full baseline, no successor overlap)
  complete  every complete four-year trajectory; quality flags enter as controls
"""
import csv
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from app.analysis import chinese_pairs as cp

OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
YEARS = cp.YEARS


def estimate(panel, level, target, year):
    x = np.array([target in o["items"][level] for o in panel], dtype=float)
    with_models = {o["car_model"] for o, v in zip(panel, x) if v}
    without_models = {o["car_model"] for o, v in zip(panel, x) if not v}
    if len(with_models) < cp.MIN_NAMEPLATES or len(without_models) < cp.MIN_NAMEPLATES:
        return None
    base = np.log([float(o["baseline_sales"]) for o in panel])
    controls = [np.ones(len(panel)), np.array([o["powertrain"] == "NEV" for o in panel], float),
                (base - base.mean()) / (base.std() or 1.0)]
    cal = sorted({int(o[f"year_{year}"]) for o in panel})
    controls += [np.array([int(o[f"year_{year}"]) == c for o in panel], float) for c in cal[1:]]
    flags = sorted(set().union(*(o["quality"][year] for o in panel)))
    controls += [np.array([f in o["quality"][year] for o in panel], float) for f in flags]
    basis, rank = cp._column_basis(np.column_stack(controls))
    xr = x - basis @ (basis.T @ x)
    info = float(xr @ xr)

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

The article is dated **August 14, 2018** (2018-08-14, 10:00:41).

Yes, it reports that the EA211 1.5L naturally aspirated engine will replace the 1.4L and 1.6L powertrains in the Santana lineup in China. The article says the current-generation Santana was unveiled in China in **2012**.

Key sentence:
> "原廠代號EA211的1.5升自然進氣引擎將會取代中國市場Volkswagen Santana車系中原有1.4升、1.6升動力單元"

**Article date:** The article was published on **October 17, 2018, at 15:53**. The "2026/10/13" timestamp at the bottom of the page is likely when the page was captured, not when the article was written.

**Launch date:** The article says the car "将于今晚正式上市" ("will officially launch tonight"), so the launch was the evening of October 17, 2018.

**Wheelbase change:** The wheelbase is 2973mm, which is "轴距加长100mm" (100mm longer) than the standard model. The overall length grew by 104mm and the height dropped by 16mm.

**Newly added or changed:**
- **Rear legroom:** The article says rear legroom "有着肉眼可见的增加" ("visibly increased").
- **Rear badge:** An "L" was added behind the rear badge.
- **Door storage:** The door storage dividers went from one to two.

The article says the exterior, interior, and powertrain carry over, including the 2.0T engine and 9AT gearbox. It also notes that the exterior style kits and wheel designs continue from the current model.

**Article date:** The article was published on **2018-03-27 at 10:40**. The "2026/10/13" timestamp at the bottom of the page is likely when the page was captured, not the article date.

**Launch:** The article reports that the 325T has already gone on sale. It says the news came from Chevrolet's official sources, and it gives no specific launch day. The guide prices are 10.49万 yuan for the 欣悦版 and 11.49万 yuan for the 欣尚版.

**Engine:** The 325T uses a "1.0T三缸发动机" (1.0T three-cylinder engine), rated at 120 horsepower with 165 N·m of peak torque.

**Gearbox:** It pairs with a "6速湿式双离合变速箱" (6-speed wet dual-clutch transmission).

**Date:** The article was published on **September 10, 2017** (2017-09-10). It announces the 2018 model year Vezel launch.

**New changes stated in the article** (all focus on the 1.5L version):

input.message:
## Result
Publication-eligible nameplates went from **23 to 49**. Estimated items are still **0 at every level** (feature, subcategory and category, both before and after). The cause has changed. Before, it was too few treated nameplates; now it is mainly the 95% interval gate in years 3 and 4. Years 1 and 2 now mostly pass.

I added 26 SRNI series (pairs FY210–FY235) and all 26 are publication-eligible. The run went in three batches. After each batch I ran `four_year_seeds`, then `chinese_pairs`, then `pytest`. Every pytest run showed only the 2 failures you flagged, which pin live counts (`test_live_impact_taxonomy_maps_every_news_topic`: 99 vs now 161; `test_planner_contract_ranks_news_features_from_real_sources`: validPairCount == 200). 47 passed, 1 skipped. I did not change tests, estimator code, gates, the frontend, or `bundle_exploratory.py`. Nothing is committed.

Summary now: 298 pairs, 234 valid four-year pairs, 161 independent observations, 49 eligible observations and 49 eligible nameplates.

## How the data was added
- I followed the existing mechanism exactly. Rows were added to the `SRNI_SALES` dict and as `SRNI_UPDATES.extend([...])` blocks ("Fourth/Fifth/Sixth block") in `W/backend/app/analysis/srni_panel.py`, and to `series_map` in `W/data/external/chinese_pairs/srni_car_manifest.json`. The CSVs were then regenerated with `uv run python -m app.analysis.four_year_seeds`, never edited by hand.
- I checked the raw file hash before use. My yearly sums from the raw file exactly match the existing values for Boyue, Haval H9 and Bora. All reading was done with `python3 -I` scripts in the scratchpad.
- An extra strictness rule beyond the existing pairs: the SRNI baseline year and years 1–4 must all have 12 reported months. No imputation.

## Year 1–4 estimates (none fully identified; % impact [95% CI], log SE)
| Item | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 SE | Year 4 SE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category: Energy & Charging (8 nameplates) | +54% [-9, 160], 0.27 | +98% [11, 255], 0.30 | 0.40 | 0.51 |
| Category: Smart Exterior (17) | +4% [-34, 64] | +23% [-27, 107] | +22% [-34, 124], SE 0.31 | 0.43 |
| Category: Connected Ecosystem (9) | +9% [-38, 91] | +25% [-26, 112] | +18%, SE 0.345 | 0.53 |
| Category: Vehicle Dynamics (29) | -12% [-46, 45] | +5% [-38, 78] | +5%, SE 0.33 | 0.53 |
| Subcategory: ride_body_control (8) | +81% [15, 184] | +172% [56, 375] | 0.40 | 0.63 |
| Subcategory: by_wire_controls (5) | -38% [-62, -0.3] | -31% [-63, 31] | 0.353 | 0.48 |
| Feature: Advanced driver assistance (13) | +30% [-16, 102] | +37% [-19, 134] | +10%, SE 0.35 | 0.53 |
| Feature: Larger or extra displays (14) | -14% [-41, 26] | -5% [-39, 49] | +12%, SE 0.335 | 0.51 |

Year-4 SEs are now 0.43–1.15, down from 1.0–2.0. Reaching the 0.35 cutoff needs roughly 2–4 times more eligible nameplates.

## Changan CS35 removed after integration
It was researched and integrated, then taken out. Launched 2017-03-16, it was the only eligible observation with calendar year 2017, so its own year dummy had leverage 1.0. That tripped the high-leverage gate on every item. Without it, year-1/2 SEs drop to about 0.19–0.35. It can come back once other January–March 2017 launches are documented.

## New pairs
- FY210 Audi A6L 2019-01-15
- FY211 VW Sagitar 2019-03-18
- FY212 Buick LaCrosse 2019-03-28
- FY213 Honda Crider 2018-09-27
- FY214 Ford Focus 2018-11-08
- FY215 Volvo XC60 2017-12-20
- FY216 Kia Sportage 2018-04-16
- FY217 Nissan Tiida 2018-11-15
- FY218 Hyundai Verna 2017-09-19
- FY219 Changan CS15 2019-03-21
- FY220 Maxus G10 2017-09
- FY221 Mercedes-Benz E-Class 2019-03
- FY222 Honda Odyssey 2018-07-15
- FY223 Geely Vision X6 2018-06-01
- FY224 Roewe i6 2019-03-29
- FY225 BMW X1 2018-10-15
- FY226 Ford Escort 2018-10-22
- FY227 Chevrolet Cavalier 2018-03
- FY228 Skoda Superb 2019-02-27
- FY229 Nissan Murano 2018-07
- FY230 Skoda Rapid 2018-09-17
- FY231 Mercedes-Benz GLC (GLC L) 2018-10-17
- FY232 Ford Edge 2017-10
- FY233 VW Santana 2018-08
- FY234 Honda Vezel 2017-09-10
- FY235 Dongfeng Fengxing Lingzhi 2018-09

## Sources and judgement calls to review
- **Thin bundles (1–2 features):** Rapid, Santana, Vezel, Lingzhi, Edge, Superb (powertrain/emissions only), Cavalier.
- **Santana:** the source is kingautos.net (Taiwan), dated 2018-08-14, and reports the 1.5L "will replace" the old engines. The launch month is therefore approximate.
- **Sources that are not a launch-day article:**
  - Vision X6 and Odyssey come from pre-launch articles that name the launch day.
  - Cavalier, Murano and E-Class articles say "recently launched", so only the month is known.
- **Roewe i6:** the launch date comes from a later autohome article (2019-06-06).
- **Maxus G10 Plus:** the SAIC release says it launches at the 2017 Chengdu show, so I used 2017-09.
- **Facelifts and new powertrain variants inside the windows were not recorded as successors.** This matches how the existing 30 SRNI pairs were handled. I only skipped a series when a full new generation fell in the window. Known in-window facelifts: Magotan-style mid-cycle updates on BMW X1 2019-10, Superb 2019-07, Vision X6 2019-10, A6L 2022-08, Sagitar 2022-06, XC60 2021-06, Edge 2019-08, Odyssey hybrid 2019-04, Crider hybrid 2020-06, Rapid 2020-02, Vezel 2019-06, GLC 2019-08.
- **Lingzhi:** its baseline year 2017 contains the 2018款 facelift (2017-10).
- **Year-only `nameplate_launch` values** where the month was not verified: Audi A6L 2005, LaCrosse 2006, Focus 2005, Sportage 2010, Tiida 2005, Verna 2010, E-Class 2005, Odyssey 2002, Roewe i6 2017, Rapid 2013, Edge 2015, Santana 1983, Lingzhi 2001. They are all well before February of the baseline year.
- **Unreferenced research files:** the source research JSONs, including URLs and later-update notes, are in the scratchpad as `out_g1.json`–`out_g5.json` and `batch1-3.json`. Nothing in the repo references them.

## Series skipped
- **Fewer than 12 SRNI months in a needed year:** about 1,130 of 1,237 SRNI series, including all but 24 Chinese brands. Only 109 met the windows.
- **Full new generation inside the window:** Haval H6, Corolla, Sylphy, Levin, RAV4, Fit, ix25, Highlander, BMW 3 Series, Audi A3, Audi Q3, Mazda3, Golf, Trax, Mistra, Octavia (PRO), Roewe RX5, Kia K3, GA6, Polo, C-Class, Outlander, Geely Vision sedan.
- **SRNI series also contains the successor:**
  - Lamando (2022 volume includes 凌渡L)
  - Envision (Envision S/Plus in the same series)

## Result
Publication-eligible nameplates went from **23 to 49**. Estimated items are still **0 at every level** (feature, subcategory and category, both before and after). The cause has changed. Before, it was too few treated nameplates; now it is mainly the 95% interval gate in years 3 and 4. Years 1 and 2 now mostly pass.

I added 26 SRNI series (pairs FY210–FY235) and all 26 are publication-eligible. The run went in three batches. After each batch I ran `four_year_seeds`, then `chinese_pairs`, then `pytest`. Every pytest run showed only the 2 failures you flagged, which pin live counts (`test_live_impact_taxonomy_maps_every_news_topic`: 99 vs now 161; `test_planner_contract_ranks_news_features_from_real_sources`: validPairCount == 200). 47 passed, 1 skipped. I did not change tests, estimator code, gates, the frontend, or `bundle_exploratory.py`. Nothing is committed.

Summary now: 298 pairs, 234 valid four-year pairs, 161 independent observations, 49 eligible observations and 49 eligible nameplates.

## How the data was added
- I followed the existing mechanism exactly. Rows were added to the `SRNI_SALES` dict and as `SRNI_UPDATES.extend([...])` blocks ("Fourth/Fifth/Sixth block") in `W/backend/app/analysis/srni_panel.py`, and to `series_map` in `W/data/external/chinese_pairs/srni_car_manifest.json`. The CSVs were then regenerated with `uv run python -m app.analysis.four_year_seeds`, never edited by hand.
- I checked the raw file hash before use. My yearly sums from the raw file exactly match the existing values for Boyue, Haval H9 and Bora. All reading was done with `python3 -I` scripts in the scratchpad.
- An extra strictness rule beyond the existing pairs: the SRNI baseline year and years 1–4 must all have 12 reported months. No imputation.
